It's funny because Voat's structure mimics the idea of state's powers vs federal powers. In this case Voat does have a mandate against spam (federal level) but basically leaves it up to the subverses to define what constitutes spam (state level). I think it's a good compromise because it allows each subverse community to decide how strict they want to be and what guidelines to put in place.

For example, /v/gaming's community allows (relevant) self-promotion even by new accounts, but ongoing promotion requires demonstrating active participation in the /v/gaming community (by posting other relevant material, commenting on other voaters' posts, or starting discussion posts). Each community having the freedom to set their own spam criteria allows each community to address spam in whatever way is best for them.

Edit: I only noticed this important distinction a day later - Voat's subverse moderators are required by Voat's TOS to enforce the TOS on their subs:

Under the section "Moderators":

When you receive notice that there is content that violates this user agreement on subverses you moderate, you agree to remove it.

What makes this distinction important is that while states aren't required to enforce federal law, subs are required to enforce the site's TOS. In terms of spam this doesn't make much difference because Voat's TOS leave spam undefined, but it means mods can't ignore reported TOS violations without violating the TOS themselves.
